one_liner: Open-continuous Air Force public notice filling violence-prevention workforce roles (strategy, communications, program analysis, resilience leadership) at GS-9 to GS-15 in multiple locations.
fit_summary: Every grade's specialized experience centers on violence prevention and behavioral, social science or public health practice. Daniel's public health response work (vaccination sites, mpox response, preparedness seminars) is public health practice but not prevention programming, so GS-9 is the realistic target; related graduate study may count there, and his M.A. includes social science coursework, so ask whether it qualifies.
eligibility: Hiring path is listed as 'public,' so U.S. citizens without prior federal service may apply.

GS-9 requires one year of specialized experience equivalent to GS-07 (violence prevention; behavioral, social science or public health duties). The alternative is 2 years of graduate education, with transcripts submitted.
Higher grades require one year at the next-lower grade in violence prevention program delivery, training design or program management. GS-13 and above also require supervision or leadership of staff.
A Secret security clearance is required. You must be able to obtain one, and it does not need to be held at application.
Positions are on-site with no telework, at multiple locations. Confirm which locations, such as the Pentagon or Joint Base Andrews, are near Manassas.
keywords: behavioral, social science and/or public health practices
strategy: Target GS-9, where his M.A. may stand in for experience. Don't self-rate into GS-11 or above unless he has a year of violence-prevention program work at the next-lower grade.

Frame the IEM work around preparedness, community resilience, risk assessment and stakeholder outreach, linking it to prevention and resilience only where truthful. Spell out your actual title, dates, hours per week and duties.

Lead with his Rural Health Transformation Program tracking for KSA 2 (laws and regulations) and his exercise facilitation for federal, state and private-sector clients for KSA 4 (tact and diplomacy with high-level officials).
Add any volunteer, campaign, crisis-line or community work involving suicide, substance abuse or violence prevention. The posting explicitly credits volunteer experience.
Answer the questionnaire conservatively, because answers are checked against the resume and unsupported answers lead to 'not qualified.' Keep the resume to two pages.
The notice is open until December 2026, but announcements like this are often reviewed in batches. Apply early and upload transcripts if a graduate degree applies.
resume_bullets: Took part in public health seminars on response and recovery roles (2022–2024) and attended the APHA and National Healthcare Coalition Preparedness conferences (2022).
Supported COVID-19 vaccination and monoclonal antibody sites (2021–2022) and a state health agency's mpox response (2022–2023).
Facilitated full-scale and tabletop exercises for federal, state and private-sector clients (2022–2024).
interview_questions: Describe your experience with prevention of interpersonal or self-directed violence, such as suicide, sexual assault or substance abuse.
Tell us about a time you advised a senior official on a sensitive or controversial issue.
How would you assess whether a prevention program is meeting its objectives?
How have you developed a plan or strategy with very broad guidance and little precedent?
watch_outs: The specialized experience is narrowly focused on violence prevention and behavioral or public health practice, so emergency management alone may be rated not qualified.
A Secret clearance and no telework are required, and the actual duty locations within 'Multiple Locations' are unclear.
The duties list includes HR and budget formulation work that may differ from the prevention focus. Read each position description title carefully before applying.
